cases.justification: A permission rule is an implication and does not contradict itself, so the policy set has a model.
Independent permission implications constrain different predicates, so both can hold in one model.
The same role-action-resource predicate is required and prohibited, so the constraints cannot share a model.
The permission and prohibition impose opposite truth values on the same predicate, making the set unsatisfiable.

policy_texts: Only administrators can delete user accounts.
cases.justification: The exclusivity implication and the administrators permission agree on the permitted role, so a model exists.

policy_texts: Only administrators can delete user accounts.
cases.justification: Under the documented assumptions that roles are mutually exclusive and each named role has a witness, the guest witness is permitted to delete but cannot be an administrator, contradicting the only-role implication.
The two permission implications concern distinct role-action-resource predicates and therefore are jointly satisfiable.

policy_texts: Only auditors can read audit logs.
cases.justification: The only-role implication does not assert that an auditor exists, so it can coexist with the auditor prohibition.
The supplied administrator fact and permission implication force the conclusion, so premises with its negation are unsatisfiable.
The independent Bob auditor fact activates the supplied implication and entails reading audit logs.

policy_texts: Only administrators can delete user accounts.
cases.justification: The only-role implication has an independent Carol deletion fact as its antecedent, so Carol must be an administrator.
The supplied operator fact and permission implication entail the restart predicate for Dana.
Guest membership does not establish administrator membership, so a model can satisfy the premises while negating the conclusion.
The auditor fact concerns reading, not exporting, so the premises have a countermodel in which export is false.
An implication alone does not assert its antecedent, so the conclusion is not entailed and a countermodel exists.
The premises entail the negation of the requested permission, so they are satisfiable with the positive conclusion false.
